evidence.positive: Injected real Epic SIU^S14 messages into the mayo-mayo tenant via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send against localhost:49985. Case OR2782P1: an In Room SIU (SCH-20 sender 9101 'OPTIME PERIOP NURSE', AIP anesthesia rows unstaffed) created the case and mayo-mayo.operations.primary_practitioner_id resolved to practitioner epic_user_id=9101 'PERIOP OPTIME'. A following Anes Start SIU for the same case, still sent by 9101 but with AIP-4 role 2.10 staffed by PERID 7001 ANESDOC^ALICE, overwrote it: the row became epic_user_id=7001 'ALICE ANESDOC', last_modified_date 2026-08-27 18:40:36.351, and the app logged 'Anes Start attributed to the AIP roster's highest-ranked anesthesia clinician role=2.10 caseId=OR2782P1'. Reproduced end to end on a second case (OR2782RESTORE) after the class-swap restore. Rank order verified on OR2782RANK (roster staffed with Resident 2.60, CRNA 2.20, SRNA 2.100): CRNA 7020 'CHRIS CRNA' won, log 'role=2.20'. Sender-in-roster branch verified on OR2782SENDER: an Anes Start sent by resident PERID 7060 who is himself on the AIP roster kept the sender (7060 'RITA RESIDENT') even though attending 7001 was rostered at 2.10, log 'Anes Start attributed to its own sender, who the AIP roster staffs in an anesthesia role.' On demo-demo, POST /api/app-launch as loopuser on staged case 91980 set primary_practitioner to 'LOOP CLINICIAN'.
evidence.negative: Case OR2782N1: Anes Start arrived first (AIP 2.10 = PERID 7002 ANESDOC^BOB) and attributed 7002 'BOB ANESDOC' at 18:40:57.678. A later In Room SIU for the same case from a different sender (9103 'OPTIME OTHER NURSE') did NOT displace it - the row still read epic_user_id=7002 with last_modified_date unchanged at 2026-08-27 18:40:57.678, so no write occurred at all. Separately on OR2782REDFLIP2: after an In Room seeded 9105 'SEED OPTIME', a second In Room from sender 9106 carrying PERID 7004 ANESDOC^CAROL at AIP 2.10 left the row at 9105 'SEED OPTIME', timestamp unchanged - In Room never overwrites even when it names an anesthesia clinician. On OR2782EMPTYAIP, an Anes Start whose AIP anesthesia rows named nobody kept the existing In Room attribution 9101 'PERIOP OPTIME' and logged 'Anes Start named no anesthesia clinician in AIP - keeping the sender'.
evidence.red_check: Two independent red checks, both reverted and both re-verified green afterwards. (1) Pre-fix class swap: compiled the parent commit's HL7ProcessingContext, DefaultHL7ProcessingContext and MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessor (lombok on the compile classpath only) and copied them into /app/classes, which precedes /app/libs on the container classpath, then restarted. The app booted clean ('Started OrciApplication in 13.175 seconds'). Sending In Room then Anes Start for a fresh case OR2782PREFIX left mayo-mayo.operations.primary_practitioner_id NULL - no 'Anes Start attributed...' line was logged at all, which is exactly the pre-fix defect. Restored the backed-up shipped classes (sha1 e13f27b26d57711de27d44eca831e30867acbfbd matched the pre-swap backup), removed the two shadow files added under /app/classes/com/guided/orci/integration, restarted, and re-ran the positive on OR2782RESTORE, which again attributed 7001 'ALICE ANESDOC'. (2) Data flip on OR2782REDFLIP2: took the exact In Room message that had just failed to overwrite and changed only the event name in ZCS-3 and the OBX-3 identifier from 'In Room' to 'Anes Start' (diff of the two saved fixtures shows only those two lines plus the message control id). The absence assertion went red immediately - the attribution moved from 9105 'SEED OPTIME' to 7004 'CAROL ANESDOC' at 18:42:19.779, logging 'Anes Start attributed to the AIP roster's highest-ranked anesthesia clinician role=2.10 caseId=OR2782REDFLIP2'. Reverting the input back to In Room and re-sending left the row untouched. (3) Also flipped the OperationService.startOperation hunk alone: recompiled the shipped source with only the OR-2782 hunk reverted to the old fill-if-null guard, swapped the single class in, and confirmed that a second app-launch as admin on demo case 91980 (already owned by LOOP CLINICIAN) did NOT take it over; restored the original class (sha1 7fa697739c4942d83872d227af99d288bd1df95b) and the same launch then did re-attribute to 'ADMIN CLINICIAN'.

caveats: Epic OAuth is not configured in this instance, so every case-start event failed downstream with 'Epic OAuth is not enabled - keys not configured'; the attribution itself is written by saveOperation before that point and was unaffected, but the Mayo case-start path through OperationService.startOperation could not be reached here.
The OperationService.startOperation change was therefore exercised on demo-demo via /api/app-launch rather than through a Mayo timing event.

That change is not fill-if-null-preserving as the commit message states: with a user present it is now an unconditional overwrite for every tenant, so a second clinician launching an already-attributed case takes ownership. Confirmed at runtime by flipping the hunk. It is covered by OperationServiceTest.launchingClinicianIsAttributedOutright_caseStartOnlyFills, so it reads as intended, but the commit message understates it.

When the Anes Start is sent by a rostered trainee, that trainee is attributed over a rostered attending (verified on OR2782SENDER). This follows the ticket wording ('clinician who clicks anesthesia start') but conflicts with the ANESTHESIA_ROLE_CODES ranking rationale; worth a product confirmation if attending-level attribution is what Mayo reporting expects.
Practitioners here are skeletons - no FHIR enrichment - so practitioners.role stayed null throughout; the analytics dimension that keys on role could not be observed.
The concurrency claim behind the guarded UPDATE statements (two SIU messages for one case processed at once) was not reproduced; messages were injected sequentially.
The analytics file in the diff (error_rate_by_practitioner_role.sql) is a comment-only change with no runtime surface here.

automation.assessment: Unit coverage shipped with the change is strong and lives in CI-running *Test classes: MayoHL7SiuCaseSchedulingProcessorTest covers every branch I exercised by hand (rank order, independent CRNA above resident, sender-in-roster, PERID-not-PROVID/NPI, unresolvable attending abandons the overwrite, empty roster keeps the sender, In Room fills only, non-case-start attributes nobody), and OperationServiceTest covers the launcher-outright/case-start-fills split. The real gap is that the two tests pinning the database-level semantics - DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSaveOperationIntegrationTest and DefaultHL7ProcessingContextPractitionerRaceIntegrationTest - are named *IntegrationTest, which the root pom's surefire config excludes by default and no CI workflow runs. The guarded-UPDATE and concurrency behaviour that the whole design rests on is therefore unverified on every build. qa-suite has no SIU/HL7 scheduling family at all, so there is no end-to-end guard either.
proposed_tests: Get the two *IntegrationTest classes for this path into a job that actually runs, or split their non-Testcontainers assertions into *Test classes, so the guarded UPDATE and the race are covered on every build.

Repository test: updatePrimaryPractitionerIfNotSet must not touch a row whose primary_practitioner_id is already set, and neither statement may match a same-caseId row belonging to a different patient.
Processor test: an In Room SIU that arrives after Anes Start leaves primary_practitioner and last_modified_date both untouched (assert the timestamp, not just the practitioner).
Processor test: an Anes Start sent by a rostered trainee attributes the trainee over a rostered attending - pin the current intent so the ranking comparator cannot silently take it back.

qa-suite supplemental spec in a new SIU family: inject In Room then Anes Start through the HL7 admin send endpoint and assert the case's primary practitioner via the API, plus the reverse order as the negative.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An In Room SIU attributed the perioperative nurse who sent it, and a following Anes Start SIU replaced that with the highest-ranked anesthesia clinician named on the case's AIP roster.
Negative: With Anes Start arriving first, a later In Room from a different sender left the anesthesia attribution and its timestamp untouched.
Red check: Running the parent commit's classes in the container left the case with no primary practitioner at all, and separately flipping only the event name on an In Room message to Anes Start moved the attribution; both were reverted and the fixed behavior re-confirmed.

Automation: Branch coverage already ships with the change, but the two tests pinning the database-level write semantics are named IntegrationTest and no CI job runs them.
